---
title: "S3 - Demand model (Stage A)"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/00_utils/notebook_setup.R")
```

**Stage:** S3 (demand).
**Purpose:** build the daily crop-water demand envelope and convert it to
claims/day through the unit wall.
**Inputs:** `output/catchment_table.csv` (for the gauge list), raw CAMELS-IND
forcing via `R/00_utils/io.R`.
**Outputs:** none (worked example + assertions).
**Parameters:** `P$sowing_doy`, `P$season_length`, `P$kc_base`, `P$kc_peak`,
`P$kc_off`, `P$phi`, `P$d_mm`.

## Equation

`[assumption]` Demand is the crop-water envelope

```
need_mm(t) = max(Kc(doy) * PET0(t) - phi * P(t), 0)
lambda(t) = need_mm(t) / d
```

with a kharif `Kc` curve, `phi = 0.7` effective rain, and claim depth
`d = 20 mm`. PET0 is GLEAM PET (Hargreaves with the 0.408 radiation
conversion is the predeclared alternative, swept in S8).

## Worked example: first selected gauge

```{r}
ct <- nb_require("catchment_table.csv", "S3")
g <- ct$gauge_id[1]
f <- .read_forcing_one(g)
nb_assert(!is.null(f), sprintf("no forcing file for gauge %d", g))

pet <- f$pet_gleam_mm
if (anyNA(pet)) {
  ra <- extraterrestrial_radiation(ct$lat[1], as.integer(format(f$date, "%j")))
  hg <- hargreaves_et0(f$tmax_c, f$tmin_c, f$tavg_c, ra)
  pet[is.na(pet)] <- hg[is.na(pet)]
}
doy <- as.integer(format(f$date, "%j"))
kc <- kc_curve(doy)
need <- crop_need_mm(kc * pet, f$prcp_mm, P$phi)
lambda <- demand_claims(need, P$d_mm)

nb_assert(all(need >= 0, na.rm = TRUE), "negative crop need")
nb_assert(all(abs(lambda - need / P$d_mm) < 1e-12, na.rm = TRUE),
          "lambda must equal need / d")
cat(sprintf("gauge %d: mean need %.3f mm/day, mean lambda %.4f claims/day\n",
            g, mean(need, na.rm = TRUE), mean(lambda, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

```{r fig-demand}
mon <- data.table(date = f$date, lambda = lambda)[
  , .(lambda = mean(lambda, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")))]
ggplot(mon, aes(month, lambda)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12) +
  labs(x = "calendar month", y = "mean demand (claims/day)",
       title = sprintf("Gauge %d: seasonal demand envelope", g)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

`[measurement]` The seasonal peak sits inside the kharif window; demand is
zero when rain exceeds crop water use. Demand is a *depth rate*, so it is
independent of catchment area by construction -- the gauge dependence enters
through supply and the catchment-relative queue thresholds.
